note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a Const 19, NIC 53, Execute Decree 31/2012 112, 125; A06b Const 19, NIC 53, Execute Decree 31/2012 112, 125; L05 Const 20, NIC 47, 64): ordinary naturalisation after 4 years' residence; the applicant must give up other citizenships (with major exceptions); a citizen keeps it on taking another (loss applies only to naturalised citizens, not modelled). Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generally applicable provision), A02a (birth in country: Generally applicable provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: by birth in the territory unconditionally; by descent from either parent, with no further limit on a child born abroad. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Nicaragua, 2024
sources.said: Person has been resident in Nicaragua for a continuous period of 4 years since being granted a permanent resident permit. ... Renunciation of citizenship of another country required (except if person is a national by birth of Spain or a Central American country (see A18). ... Person is a citizen by naturalisation who voluntarily acquires citizenship of another country. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born in Nicaragua to a citizen. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born abroad to a citizen. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born in Nicaragua. Unless born to foreign diplomats, foreign employees of international organizations, or those sent by their national governments to work in Nicaragua. ... No provision
